Chapter 136: 0133 CCTV's "Dialogue" Airs (Extra chapter for Alliance Leader Tarot Club Cleaner)

The day before CCTV's "Dialogue" aired, Bian Guanyue came to Hangcheng to see her cousin.

Her cousin was named Jona. She was tall and slender, with very short hair, looking like a tomboy.

"Here, this is the place I'm renting." Jona led Bian Guanyue from the station to an old residential complex.

It was a one-bedroom, one-living room apartment with a kitchen and bathroom. Clothes were piled everywhere in the living room and bedroom.

Bian Guanyue looked around carefully. "Didn't you used to sell digital products?"

Jona shook her head repeatedly. "The competition is too fierce. If I sell knockoffs, the Taobao shops in Shencheng get their stock from Huaqiangbei, and their cost price is 10 to 30% lower than mine in Hangcheng. If I sell authentic products, all those counter vendors on Wensan Lu in Hangcheng have opened their own Taobao shops. How could I possibly compete with them?"

"Is selling clothes going well?" Bian Guanyue asked.

Jona said, "It's okay for now. Thanks to the influence of K-dramas, Korean-style clothing is the hottest seller right now. High-quality imitation Adidas and Nike shoes also sell very well."

To put it bluntly, she was just a seller of knockoffs.

Bian Guanyue asked, "With you looking after your Taobao shop, how do you have time to go to your classes at school?"

"I skip half and attend half. The Taobao shop doesn't need to be watched every single second," Jona sighed. "Sigh, I'll probably fail two-thirds of my courses this semester."

Bian Guanyue said, "He's pretty much the same as you."

Jona's spirits suddenly lifted. "Did you really... you know... do it with him?"

"What are you talking about?" Bian Guanyue feigned ignorance.

"Forget it if you don't want to talk about it," Jona said, flopping onto the sofa. "Find a place to sit yourself. I'm not waiting on you."

The sofa was also piled with clothes and shoes, leaving no place to sit.

Bian Guanyue moved a bundle of clothes aside and sat down carefully amidst the pile. "You've stocked up so much. Business must be great."

Jona said smugly, "Of course. Don't look down on the fact that I sell imitations, I care about quality too. The profit margin might be a bit lower, but I'm getting more and more repeat customers. My sales have gone up again this month. I estimate my net profit will break 4,000 yuan! That's net profit, mind you, not sales revenue or gross profit. I've deducted rent and internet fees."

"That's very impressive," Bian Guanyue complimented her.

She had thought her cousin was earning over ten thousand a month, which was why she couldn't even attend her classes, but it turned out her monthly profit was only 4,000 yuan. And she had only recently started earning this much; she used to make even less each month.

Jona was full of ambition. "Once my monthly income exceeds ten thousand, I'll hire another employee and expand the business. I'm going to be the Taobao Queen!"

Bian Guanyue then brought up the matter of helping to sell Legends of the Three Kingdoms.

"I don't have to stock or ship anything, and I get a 15% commission just for helping to sell?" Jona thought she had misheard.

Bian Guanyue said, "That's what he said."

"Then I'll definitely do it. It's free money, stupid not to take it." Jona was very happy.

After the release of the Wind expansion pack, the physical cards for "Legends of the Three Kingdoms" were printed more exquisitely, and each set now sold for 40 yuan. Due to mass printing, although there were 10 more cards, the printing cost had actually decreased.

After deducting the 12 yuan printing cost, the 6 yuan commission for the Taobao shop, the 7 to 10 yuan for delivery fees, and then deducting warehouse and labor costs, Chen Guiliang made a few yuan from selling one set of Legends of the Three Kingdoms.

In fact, as long as he wasn't losing money, Chen Guiliang was willing to sell them this way.

The two cousins had dinner together that night, and the next day they went to see West Lake and other scenic spots. Bian Guanyue had a wonderful time.

Her cousin was her aunt's daughter, and they had been close since childhood, even closer than real sisters.

After a day of sightseeing, they returned in the afternoon. Jona checked the orders on her online store, and Bian Guanyue helped her cousin pack and ship them.

After dinner, Bian Guanyue asked, "Does this TV work?"

"I don't know," Jona said. "I've been renting this place for half a year and I've never turned on the TV. Why do you want to watch TV?"

"Hee hee, he's on a show, and it's airing tonight," Bian Guanyue said with a sweet smile.

Jona said disdainfully, "Men are all unreliable. Look at your dad's situation, and look at my dad's. Don't you forget. Chen Guiliang has started a company now. When he becomes a big boss, he'll definitely be just like my dad. One at home, and who knows how many outside."

"He won't," Bian Guanyue said.

"Sigh, you never used to be like this," Jona said. "Let me tell you, a woman has to rely on herself, to have her own career and life. You can't rely on anyone but yourself. I figured this out a long time ago!"

Bian Guanyue smiled but didn't reply.

Jona went over to turn on the TV. Something wasn't plugged in right, and there was no signal on the screen. While fiddling with the TV, she said, "When I first switched to selling clothes and shoes, I worked myself to death just to earn three or four hundred a month. Do I need that little bit of living money? It's all for the sake of building a career!"

"Mmm, you're really amazing, cousin," Bian Guanyue said.

Jona continued to expound on her philosophy: "When we have money, we won't have to put up with men's attitudes. Love is bullshit, it's all fake. Only money is real. By the time you graduate, I'll probably have started my own company. You can come help me then. I'll give you shares, and we sisters can work together to make the business big."

"Let's talk about it then. I don't know what I want to do in the future either," Bian Guanyue said.

"This stupid TV!"

Jona aimed at the top right corner of the television and smacked it hard at a 45-degree angle to the floor.

After a few slaps, the TV finally got a signal.

Jona dusted off her hands. "The old ways still work best."

It was still early; "Dialogue" wouldn't air until nine-thirty.

Jona would occasionally sit at her computer to manage her online store, and when she had a moment, she'd come to the living room to watch TV with Bian Guanyue.

"Cousin, hurry! The show is starting!" Bian Guanyue shouted.

Jona rolled her eyes and walked over. "It's just a TV show. No need to be so excited."

Bian Guanyue said, "It's his first time on TV... no, that's not right. I think he was on the Longdu City news before."

Jona sat cross-legged on the sofa and opened a bag of sunflower seeds to snack on.

The show opened with a montage, introducing Chen Guiliang in detail with text and a voiceover. A large part of the host, Miss Shen's, opening monologue had been cut in post-production.

The opening conversation between the three guests was also cut by a third.

It had nothing to do with the content; it was purely to control the runtime.

Chen Guiliang's statements appeared one after another.

I don't recommend that freshmen start a business.

But you started a business yourself.

I'm different.

How are you different?

Because I believe I can succeed.

Jona burst out laughing. "Your boyfriend is pretty bold."

"He's always been very confident," Bian Guanyue smiled.

Jona slapped her thigh. "This kid is one of my kind. My academic advisor also tried to persuade me when I was skipping classes to run my Taobao shop. But I just believed I could succeed. It was useless for anyone to try and talk me out of it. If you're not confident, what's the point of starting a business?"

A few minutes later.

Chen Guiliang was commenting on the three major portal websites, looking down on all of them, even saying that these websites were already outdated.

In half a year at most, I will get my first round of investment.

And what if no firm comes to invest?

Then that just means venture capitalists have no foresight, seeing gold on the roadside and not knowing to pick it up.

Let's make a bet. Within a year, Xiaonei.com's valuation will reach 10 million US dollars.

I won't bet.

Why?

Let me explain. He doesn't want to bet because he might lose.

Jona was dumbfounded. "This kid is even more arrogant than I am!"

Bian Guanyue corrected her, "He's not arrogant, he's confident. And he always delivers on what he says."

On the TV, the topic had already shifted to quality-oriented education.

Chen Guiliang sat next to the host, speaking eloquently, "This month, why is the media talking about quality-oriented education again? Because the Ministry of Education just announced the six key tasks for education reform and development in 2005, and one of them is to comprehensively promote quality-oriented education."

Professor Shang was a bit surprised. "You're running a company and writing a book, and you still pay attention to this stuff?"

"On the major portal websites, topics related to quality-oriented education are suddenly being hyped up. There must be a specific reason behind it," Chen Guiliang said. "The Ministry of Education's official document can be found online. You click on it, and you can finish reading it in a few minutes."

Chen Guiliang even took on the host's job, asking the studio audience, "Who knows the main content of the Ministry of Education's document?"

No one answered.
